text:
sam: Heads up — p95 jump on /v1/generate for tenant acme-inc right after runtime 3.14.5 canary started (12% traffic). Support ticket ACME-453 raised by CSM. Anyone around?

priya_oncall: I'm on. seeing p95 ~420ms -> ~700ms from 10:20 UTC, p99 also up. Can you drop the canary id?

sam: Canaries: 3.14.5 canary id c5f2. DeployBot shows rollout at 10:15 with gradual traffic.

deploybot: Deployment notice: runtime/3.14.5 -> canary c5f2 started by @release-bot at 2026-03-17T10:15:12Z. Current canary traffic: 12%.

miguel: I pulled traces. There's a tight cluster of requests showing extra queue wait before kernel selection. Sample span: kernel_selection -> queue_wait(ms): 180 -> 340ms. That's the delta. KV cache hit rate for acme-inc decreased ~15% at same time.

tasha_obs: Grafana panels: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 p95/generate and p99. Attached snapshot: p95 baseline 420ms, canary spike 700ms. KV cache hit went 78% -> 63%. Also observe more small batches (batch size distribution shifted left).

sam: Interesting — kernel version switch included "fast-attn-v2" + new scheduler tweaks. Could be more small batches + cold cache causing per-request overhead. Any recent changes to batching or kvcache eviction policy in 3.14.5?

miguel: 3.14.5 changed scheduler heuristics: prefer lower latency at expense of more frequent flushes for short tails. Also changed default inter-batch timeout from 4ms -> 1ms (intended to reduce latency for hot paths). That can reduce batching and increase kernel setup overhead.

priya_oncall: Support says customers see API p95 regressions intermittently, affects some endpoints more (short prompt loads). Could be the inter-batch timeout + cold kvcache. Any quick repro?

sam: I can repro on dev with a synthetic short-prompt workload: many 1-3 token prompts at 80 rps. Steps:
```
# repro script (simplified)
wrk -t2 -c50 -d60s --script=short_prompts.lua https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate
# observe p95/p99 via local perf plugin
```
Results: with 3.14.4 p95 ~430ms, with 3.14.5 p95 ~690ms.

miguel: Thanks. That matches logs. Also seeing kernel selection path reinitializes some per-request state more often when batch sizes are 1-2. The change to inter-batch timeout explains shift to smaller batches.

tasha_obs: Also noticed that a config flag for tenant-isolated kvcache was flipped to true for acme-inc during onboarding scripts last week — meaning their per-tenant cache is smaller. Combined with smaller batch sizes it's worse.

sam: So likely root cause = scheduler timeout change (3.14.5) + smaller tenant kvcache footprint -> lower cache hit and more kernel setup overhead -> p95 bump. Good signal.

priya_oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to 3.14.4, 2) throttle canary traffic back to 0% for acme-inc (route to stable), 3) increase inter-batch timeout remotely if we expose flag, 4) bump tenant kvcache size for acme-inc. Which is fastest?

miguel: Fastest is throttle routing for acme-inc -> send their traffic to stable. We can also cut canary % for everyone. We don't currently have a live override for inter-batch timeout per runtime without redeploy.

sam: I can open a routing override and pin acme-inc to 3.14.4 stable pool. Priya can we coordinate support message?

priya_oncall: Yes. I'll update ACME-453: We saw regression linked to recent canary rollout; routing override in progress. ETA 10m.

deploybot: Routing change: traffic_override created for tenant acme-inc -> runtime 3.14.4 at 2026-03-17T10:35:40Z by sam.

priya_oncall: After override p95 for acme-inc dropped from ~700ms -> ~430ms within 2 minutes. p99 improving too. Confirmed by Grafana.

sam: Nice. Next steps: Miguel to propose a scheduler tweak rollback or a config flag to restore inter-batch timeout behavior; Tasha to run a regression matrix across tenant cache sizes and short-prompt workloads; Priya to keep ACME updated and escalate to CSM if needed.

miguel: I'll bisect the scheduler change: two commits in 3.14.5 that touch scheduler/timeouts. Plan: revert commit A locally and run short-prompt repro; if that fixes, we can cut 3.14.6 with fix. Timeline ~2-4 hours for local bisect + staging validation.

tasha_obs: I'll schedule targeted load jobs for a few tenants (acme-inc, beta-tenant, and internal-synth) and collect batching histograms.

priya_oncall: Support note posted to ACME-453 and CSM. Will ask CSM to offer temporary routing if they request SLA credit.

sam: Add follow-ups: (a) create a postmortem doc template entry, (b) check if any other tenants saw similar but less severe deltas, (c) test reinstating larger per-tenant kvcache as mitigation.

support_bot: Ticket ACME-453 status updated: routing override applied, customer notified.

sam: Thanks all. Marking this thread for handoff — Miguel + Tasha to drive root-cause, Priya to own comms for ACME. Will re-open if canary remediation complete or if rollback needed. :white_check_mark:

miguel: quick note — running bisect now, will post results in this thread.

(edited)
